report.finding: This is Robertson's stiff test problem (k1=0.04, k2=3e7, k3=1e4 spans many orders of magnitude in rate). The model and parameters are correct - this is a genuinely stiff ODE system. CVODE was running in non-stiff (Adams/functional-iteration) mode, i.e. `integrator.stiff = False`, so it needs an enormous number of tiny internal steps to stay stable as the fast B/C dynamics kick in, and eventually exhausts `maximum_num_steps`. Raising `maximum_num_steps` just postpones the failure to a later simulation time rather than fixing the underlying issue, exactly as the user observed. Switching to the BDF/stiff mode (`integrator.stiff = True`) makes CVODE use an implicit stiff-appropriate method and the same simulation (even out to t=4e5) completes with no step-count problems.
report.evidence: With `rr.integrator.stiff` at its default `False`, `rr.simulate(0, 4e5, 200)` raises `CV_TOO_MUCH_WORK` with mxstep=20000, matching the user's error. Setting `rr.integrator.setValue('stiff', True)` and rerunning the identical call (`rr.simulate(0, 4e5, 200)`) completes successfully, ending near A≈0.0049, B≈2e-8, C≈0.995 (correct qualitative Robertson behaviour: A and B decay, C saturates near 1).

changes.what: Enabled CVODE's stiff (BDF/implicit) integration mode instead of the default non-stiff Adams mode
